tasks.short: Present policies, programmes or budgets to government committees and answer their questions.

steps.what: Confirm the committee's request, submission deadline, format and speaking arrangements.
Collect approved policy documents, budget figures and programme results.
Agree the position, requested outcome and limits on commitments with senior advisers.
Draft the presentation, speaking notes and likely questions.

loop.input: Approved hearing position, evidence pack and presentation template.
loop.output: Draft presentation, speaking notes and question brief with source references.
loop.check: Check every figure against supplied data and every citation against supplied documents; flag unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved claims become visible gaps for the adviser.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble figures, but adapting explanations and anticipating questions requires reading and writing.

steps.what: Check legal claims, confidentiality and disclosure restrictions.
Rehearse difficult answers and approve the materials for committee use.
Present the position, answer questions and make commitments within delegated authority.
Record commitments, assign follow-up owners and confirm deadlines.

loop.input: Hearing notes and explicit public commitments.
loop.output: Proposed commitment entries, owners and deadlines.
loop.check: Link each entry to a note passage; leave unstated owners or dates blank for confirmation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass; ambiguous commitments go to the chief executive.
loop.why_not_simpler: Commitments appear in varied language rather than fixed fields.

tasks.design: A reusable hearing template in {DOCS} and a configured {WORKFLOW} handle intake and deadlines. A deterministic job on {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles approved evidence from {DOCS}, {ERP} and {BI}; a bounded model drafts the presentation and question brief. Legal review, release approval and the hearing remain human, while approved commitments become tasks in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits in separate reports, while each committee needs a different explanation and careful disclosure checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports and document templates support reliable assembly. Bounded drafting can adapt the narrative while keeping figures and sources traceable.
tasks.still_hard: Political questioning, uncertain consequences and commitments made during discussion require executive judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The chief executive earns trust, reads the room and accepts responsibility for statements and commitments.

ambition.what: An evidence-linked written response service for unanswered committee questions.

tasks.altitude: Preparation takes fewer drafting sessions, leaving more time for difficult questions and stakeholder concerns. The chief executive keeps existing speaking and commitment authority; no new statutory powers arise.

reach.task: Prepare evidence on programme delivery and track hearing commitments.
reach.learn: Learn operational metric definitions, delivery constraints and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Structured papers can be drafted from management documents with prompts for missing analysis.
Apex Group reported recovering 60% of report preparation time; this vendor case does not establish hearing savings.
Source-linked drafting and deterministic figure checks are a plausible design, not a demonstrated result for this task.
Fabricated references in a government report illustrate why generated claims need source checks.

assumptions: This supplemental task arises in regulated, publicly accountable or publicly funded organisations; many mid-size companies rarely do it.
Shares estimate active work across the executive and supporting roles, excluding waiting for the hearing.
The starter can use approved file uploads before live integrations are available.
Build ranges estimate working effort for one reusable hearing format and exclude committee scheduling delays.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; national rules determine any employee consultation required by the implementation.
unknowns: How often the chief executive appears before committees.
Who can approve disclosures and commitments.
Which evidence can be exported or uploaded.
Whether hearing notes or official transcripts are available.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed tools.
research_questions: Can each budget figure retain its period, definition and source through presentation generation?
Which unsupported or misleading claims escape the proposed validation checks?
Does the reusable format save enough preparation effort at the actual hearing frequency?
new_work: Review generated explanations and anticipated questions.
Maintain evidence mappings and presentation templates.
Confirm ambiguous commitments before assigning follow-up tasks.
Maintain access restrictions and disclosure classifications.

tasks.short: Assess legislation and public policy, then recommend changes for affected groups.

steps.what: Collect relevant proposals, enacted texts, consultation deadlines and supporting guidance.
Read the texts and distinguish proposed changes, binding duties and unresolved interpretation.

loop.input: Versioned official texts, previous assessment and fixed comparison questions.
loop.output: Draft change brief with article references, effective dates and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify quotations, document versions and date fields; the legal adviser checks interpretation and omissions.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair pass per source pack; missing or conflicting text requires legal review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Text comparison finds edits but cannot reliably explain their meaning or distinguish duties from commentary.

steps.what: Map possible effects on operations, costs and affected groups.
Discuss consequences, competing interests and proposed changes with affected representatives.
Draft a recommendation explaining evidence, beneficiaries, costs and trade-offs.

loop.input: Reviewed legal brief, impact assessment, stakeholder views and policy options.
loop.output: Draft recommendation with evidence references and explicit uncertainties.
loop.check: Check cited passages and figures; distinguish stakeholder claims from verified findings and flag missing evidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved evidence gaps remain visible for executive review.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but synthesising competing arguments requires bounded reading and writing.

steps.what: Challenge the reasoning and settle the organisation's recommended position.
Approve and submit the recommendation through the required channel.

tasks.design: Configured alerts and a versioned source library in {DOCS} support a bounded comparison of official texts from {GOV_PORTAL}. A reusable generator drafts recommendations from reviewed legal findings, human impact assessments and stakeholder views. A release workflow approves the exact submission and archives its receipt; unsupported portal submission remains a human action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Legal changes require interpretation across documents, and organisational effects depend on facts that legislation does not contain.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned documents, deterministic comparisons and source-linked drafting reduce reading and composition effort without replacing legal interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous law, uneven effects on groups and uncertain policy outcomes remain difficult to validate before implementation.
tasks.human_edge: People judge whose interests count, test assumptions with affected groups and take responsibility for the recommendation.

ambition.what: An accessible policy impact briefing for small community organisations affected by proposed changes.

tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less time reconstructing legal background and more time testing consequences with affected groups. Recommendation authority stays within the existing mandate; legislative decisions remain with public authorities.

reach.task: Test proposed policy changes against operating processes and implementation costs.
reach.learn: Learn process dependencies, cost drivers and how to distinguish legal duties from policy preferences.

evidence.claim: Source-referenced answers to planning-rule questions are used with staff checking the answers.
The cross-government trial reported drafting savings, but these do not establish reliable legal interpretation.
Mapping legal changes to operational consequences needs contextual human assessment.
GDPR Article 22 limits certain solely automated decisions affecting individuals; this design does not automate those decisions.

assumptions: The company has a policy interest or public-service mandate; it does not exercise legislative authority.
Public texts are available through official alerts or approved downloads.
A legal adviser remains available to verify interpretation.
Submission automation is limited to supported channels; otherwise the workflow prepares a checked submission package.
Shares estimate active work across contributing roles rather than elapsed consultation time.
Build ranges cover one policy domain; GDPR, the EU AI Act and applicable national consultation rules remain in scope.
unknowns: Which policy domains and jurisdictions matter.
Who represents affected groups and how they can participate.
Which official sources provide stable versions or alerts.
Who has authority to release recommendations.
Whether submissions contain personal or confidential information.
Which employee consultation or access approvals are required.
research_questions: Can reviewers detect omitted exceptions as reliably as incorrect quotations?
How should proposed, enacted and effective provisions be distinguished in the brief?
What evidence is needed to support claims about effects on each affected group?
new_work: Check source versions, legal interpretation and omitted exceptions.
Maintain the policy watchlist and comparison questions.
Resolve conflicting sources and missing operational facts.
Review whether stakeholder views are represented fairly.
Maintain submission requirements and access permissions.

tasks.short: Direct support departments, resolve competing priorities and hold department heads accountable for delivery.

steps.what: Compile departmental results, budgets and service measures for executive review.
Explain variances, dependencies and decisions needed from the chief executive.

loop.input: Validated departmental metrics and department heads' written updates.
loop.output: Draft exception brief separating measured variances, reported explanations and requested decisions.
loop.check: Recalculate variances deterministically; cite each explanation to its update and have the department head verify it.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; missing explanations are returned as questions.
loop.why_not_simpler: Variance arithmetic is deterministic, but concise explanations must be drawn from varied departmental updates.

steps.what: Review performance and select issues requiring executive attention.
Discuss priorities, challenge explanations and resolve conflicts between departments.
Approve priorities, resource trade-offs and escalation decisions within the executive mandate.
Send approved instructions and record owners, deadlines and dependencies.
Review delivery progress and escalate overdue or blocked actions.

tasks.design: A deterministic dataset on {DATA_PLATFORM} joins approved departmental measures from {ERP}, {PROCUREMENT} and {CRM} into {BI}. A bounded drafting step turns department updates into a source-linked exception brief, while configured {WORKFLOW} rules move approved decisions into {PROJECT}. Executive conversations and resource decisions stay human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Departmental measures use different definitions, and emailed narratives are disconnected from decisions and action tracking.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings, validation rules and configured workflows handle most of the work. A small drafting loop can summarise updates without calculating figures or deciding priorities.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing comparable measures, discovering concealed problems and choosing between competing departmental needs remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: The chief executive challenges weak explanations, negotiates commitments and balances outcomes that no single metric captures.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on cross-department service bottlenecks between monthly operating reviews.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing packs and action updates towards resolving cross-department constraints. The chief executive can make smaller operating trade-offs sooner, within existing delegated limits.

reach.task: Coordinate resolution of cross-department service bottlenecks.
reach.learn: Learn service capacity, dependency mapping and which resource trade-offs need executive approval.

evidence.claim: Report summaries and data questions are supported today, but poor data models can produce inaccurate answers.
Planning tools can flag anomalies and generate reports; this does not demonstrate autonomous departmental direction.
A vendor case reports 12 hours a month saved on executive reporting; its method is not given.
Metric joins, variance calculations and action routing usually need deterministic technology rather than autonomous agents.
The EU AI Act identifies certain staff performance monitoring and task-allocation uses as high-risk.

assumptions: Department heads already own their budgets, operating measures and progress updates.
The initial scope uses aggregate departmental performance, without individual employee scoring or automated credit decisions.
Configured routing reproduces approved decisions and cannot independently change budgets or approve spending.
Shares include supporting preparation and executive attention, excluding passive waiting.
Build ranges assume a limited set of agreed metrics and supported exports; a starter can use approved files.
Access and consultation effort includes assessing GDPR, the EU AI Act and applicable national rules; required consultation can extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: Which departmental measures are sufficiently reliable and comparable.
Which source systems support authorised exports or connectors.
Whether existing reporting already covers these requirements.
Which decisions the chief executive can delegate to the general and operations manager.
Whether proposed views expose identifiable employee data.
Which employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which exceptions actually lead to useful operating decisions?
Can source totals, reporting periods and organisational boundaries be reconciled automatically?
Does exception-based review reveal problems earlier without hiding emerging risks?
new_work: Maintain metric definitions, mappings and reconciliation checks.
Verify department explanations and distinguish claims from established causes.
Tune exception thresholds when operating conditions change.
Resolve stale ownership, overdue actions and broken data feeds.
Reassess legal and consultation requirements before adding individual-level monitoring.

tasks.short: Refer major policy matters to authorised elected representatives for final decisions.

steps.what: Receive a major policy issue and clarify the decision requested.
Check reserved matters, delegation rules and the elected body's submission requirements.

loop.input: Policy issue record, current delegation rules and submission requirements.
loop.output: Suggested referral route with exact supporting clauses and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify cited clauses and rule versions; the governance adviser checks the proposed interpretation.
loop.stop: One classification and one repair pass; ambiguous authority always goes to the governance adviser.
loop.why_not_simpler: Checklists handle explicit thresholds, but narrative reserved matters require reading and contextual interpretation.

steps.what: Decide whether referral is needed and settle the recommendation within delegated authority.
Assemble the recommendation, options, costs and supporting evidence into the required referral paper.
Check procedural completeness, financial references and confidential material before submission.
Obtain release approval and submit the referral to the authorised elected body.
Explain the referral and answer questions while elected representatives retain the final decision.
Record referral status and route clarification requests to responsible advisers.

tasks.design: A configured referral register in {WORKFLOW} tracks issues, required documents and release approval. A bounded source-linked check helps the governance adviser interpret delegation rules, while a deterministic generator assembles existing recommendations and figures from {DOCS} and {ERP}. Approved referrals use the authorised submission channel, and {PROJECT} tracks clarification requests without making the elected body's decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral rules sit in narrative governance documents, while papers, approvals and follow-up are handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured forms and document assembly remove repeated administration. A bounded clause-reading loop can suggest routes for expert checking.
tasks.still_hard: Constitutional authority, politically sensitive framing and disagreements over reserved matters require human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The chief executive recognises matters that need democratic authority and explains recommendations without pre-empting the final decision.
tasks.altitude: The chief executive spends less time checking referral completeness and chasing status. Decision rights do not change: elected representatives retain final authority over reserved matters.

reach.task: Assess delivery implications of policy options before referral.
reach.learn: Learn governance boundaries, implementation dependencies and how to present feasible alternatives.

evidence.claim: Structured management papers can be generated from existing documents.
Source-referenced rule answers with staff checking provide a relevant pattern, not proof of reliable governance routing.
Referral registers, completeness checks and approved document routing can use configured workflows and deterministic assembly.
Interpreting reserved powers and making final policy decisions remain human responsibilities in this proposed design.

assumptions: This task applies to a public-sector body or enterprise whose governance genuinely reserves matters to elected representatives.
It is not typical of an ordinary private company; its board is not treated as an elected body.
Recommendations and options already exist before referral-paper assembly; the generator does not invent policy.
The model suggests a route but cannot decide whether statutory referral is required.
Shares cover active referral preparation and explanation, excluding elected deliberation and waiting for a decision.
Build ranges cover one elected body's procedure; access, GDPR, the EU AI Act and applicable national consultation rules must be assessed.
unknowns: Whether elected representatives have any decision authority over this organisation.
Which matters are reserved and which governance texts are authoritative.
Who approves referral release and confidential annexes.
Which submission channel the elected body accepts.
Whether oral explanation is normally required.
Which access and employee consultation approvals apply.
research_questions: Can clear threshold rules resolve most routing cases without a model?
Which ambiguous reserved matters require specialist legal interpretation?
Can the released document be tied to its exact approval and submission receipt?
new_work: Maintain delegation rules, recipient details and referral templates.
Review ambiguous route suggestions and outdated clauses.
Check generated papers for completeness and disclosure errors.
Reconcile submission receipts and outstanding clarification requests.

role.altitude: The chief executive gains preparation time and earlier visibility of operating issues. The week centres more on trade-offs, stakeholder conversations and accountable decisions; board, statutory and elected decision rights remain unchanged.
reach: Work with the general and operations manager to test policy options against delivery constraints.
Use shared operating evidence to resolve cross-department bottlenecks sooner.
Connect public commitments and policy recommendations to named delivery owners.
skills_to_grow: Challenge metric definitions, source quality and unsupported causal claims.
Distinguish generated summaries from verified legal interpretation.
Frame policy trade-offs clearly for affected groups.
Design precise release gates and delegation boundaries.
Recognise when employee data use changes legal or consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Build a regular evidence-to-decision rhythm connecting departmental delivery, stakeholder concerns and policy choices, with clear human authority at each consequential action.
